rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Meta-frame lectures are closers, not openers; demo/ceiling/permission-giving lectures can open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Three openers in `## Start here` (the-2-frontiers, story-of-module-6, quality-is-grounding) are each self-certified opener-shaped in their own Meta blocks: the-2-frontiers ('Role: opener. Recap + horizon. Does not teach a new term'), story-of-module-6 ('permission-giving, not credibility-performance... Goes first because permission works before the work, not after'), quality-is-grounding ('3–5 min stakes-setter... placed early... Sets the quality-arc stakes before the build move'; explicitly WHY-vs-WHAT split against its paired closer the-loop-has-a-name, which owns naming eval). Four closers in `## Human close` (composing-the-workflow, the-loop-has-a-name, the-map-filled-in, agents-that-build-agents) are each recognition-first against material the student just built: composing-the-workflow opens 'You have a kit now... look at what composition actually is, on the run you already sailed'; the-loop-has-a-name opens 'Look at what you just shipped'; the-map-filled-in is self-certified 'Consolidation and recognition, NOT new teaching (check_lectures §1)'; agents-that-build-agents opens 'The map you just drew ended on a dashed loop, yours to draw solid' — pure callback. No opener teaches a framework-with-reasons ahead of the exercise; no closer introduces unearned vocabulary.

M6's contracted mood is practitioner fluency (encode phase of test→learn→encode), not a contrast-mood module in the rule's own M5-style sense — M4/M5 already ran the contrast this module reads from. Total opener dosage before the exercise is ~12–16 min across three short lectures (2 min / 7–9 min / 3–5 min), none of which map frameworks to problems or explain tradeoffs-with-reasons ahead of the exercise; they arm (recap, permission, stakes) rather than teach ahead.
